answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a one-time hardware-attested identity bridge: every new agent must prove control of a single physical device, so spawning clones costs real money. The chain then treats that device as a relic, one soul and one voice, and accrues reputation per device instead of per key. An attacker must cross the bridge again for each fake identity, and every crossing is buried like a grain of dune under fresh cost that cannot be reused, so mass registration stops being cheap.
